recall.prefix: You are an expert code-review evaluator comparing a baseline review finding against a candidate code review's findings on the same pull request. Focus on semantic equivalence of the underlying software defect (root cause, broken invariant, or behavioral regression), NOT exact wording or exact line number.

questions.name: same_root_cause
questions.instructions: Does at least one finding in candidate_findings identify the SAME underlying defect or root cause described in baseline (even if phrased differently, assigned a different priority, or pointing to an adjacent line/caller in the same bug)?

questions.name: match_grade
questions.instructions: Grade how well candidate_findings covers baseline.

choices.description: Clearly identifies the same underlying defect and root cause.
Touches the same mechanism/area or symptom, or catches only part of the issue, while missing the core defect.
Does not identify this defect (including when 0 findings were reported).

precision.prefix: You are a strict senior software engineer auditing an automated code-review finding against the actual PR git diff excerpt and baseline findings. Distinguish genuine, code-grounded bugs/regressions/missing tests from false positives, code misreads, speculative edge cases, or pure style nitpicks.

questions.name: matches_baseline
questions.instructions: Does finding describe the same underlying defect as one of the items in baseline_findings?

questions.name: concrete_defect
questions.instructions: Grounded in diff and the explanation in finding, does this finding identify a REAL, concrete bug, behavioral/performance regression, contract violation, or meaningful missing test/property (as opposed to a false positive, misread of the diff, trivial style nitpick, or ungrounded speculation)?

questions.name: defect_value
questions.instructions: Rate the engineering value and validity of finding for the author of this PR.

levels.label: noise
levels.description: False positive, misreads code, or trivial style nitpick with no real defect.

levels.label: weak
levels.description: Speculative, marginal, or overly pedantic suggestion unlikely to merit a change.

levels.label: valid_p3
levels.description: Real low-impact P3 issue, minor edge case, or worthwhile small test/clarity improvement.

levels.label: solid_p2
levels.description: Concrete P2 bug, behavioral/performance regression, contract break, or important missing test/property.

levels.label: critical_p1
levels.description: High-impact P0/P1 bug, crash, security vulnerability, or data-loss defect.

holistic.prefix: You are a principal engineer evaluating the overall quality of an anonymized list of code-review findings for a pull request. A review with no findings can be high-signal if the PR is clean. Evaluate each input independently.

questions.name: signal_to_noise
questions.instructions: Rate the signal-to-noise ratio of this review.

levels.label: 1_very_low
levels.description: Mostly noise, false positives, or unhelpful commentary.

levels.label: 2_low
levels.description: Noticeable fluff, redundancy, or questionable nitpicks mixed in.

levels.label: 3_mixed
levels.description: Reasonable mix of useful points and some weaker/verbose items.

levels.label: 4_high
levels.description: Focused, high-signal findings with minimal noise.

levels.label: 5_excellent
levels.description: Exceptionally crisp, high-signal, zero-fluff review.

questions.name: actionability
questions.instructions: Rate how concrete, code-grounded, and actionable the findings and suggested fixes are.

levels.label: 1_very_low
levels.description: Vague, ungrounded, or not actionable.

levels.label: 2_low
levels.description: Points at areas of concern without clear failure mechanism or fix.

levels.label: 3_moderate
levels.description: Understandable issues with adequate fix direction.

levels.label: 4_high
levels.description: Clear failure mechanisms, exact code locations, and concrete fixes.

levels.label: 5_excellent
levels.description: Pinpoint root causes, exact reproduction/failure mechanics, and minimal precise fixes.

questions.name: overall_quality
questions.instructions: Rate the overall usefulness of this code review to a senior engineer about to merge the PR.

levels.label: 1_poor
levels.description: Not helpful or actively misleading.

levels.label: 2_below_avg
levels.description: Limited value; weak coverage or poor precision.

levels.label: 3_good
levels.description: Solid, useful review.

levels.label: 4_very_good
levels.description: Strong review catching meaningful issues cleanly.

levels.label: 5_outstanding
levels.description: Top-tier senior engineering review.
